name: Salons and Spas
h1: AI Phone Agent for Salons and Spas: Appointment Booking While You Work
metaDescription: Calldesk answers salon and spa calls: service bookings, stylist preferences, reschedules and cancellation-policy questions while your hands are busy.
intro: Stylists, colorists and massage therapists cannot answer a phone with foamy gloves, a half-finished color or a client on the table. A salon's calls therefore pile up when it is busiest, and the callers are people who want to book right now, usually while on a lunch break or in the evening after work. Requests are specific: a balayage with a particular stylist, a cut for a child, a deep-tissue massage on Saturday afternoon, a bridal party trial. Reschedules and cancellations come in constantly, and a late cancellation is a lost hour that could have been filled if someone had answered and offered it. Questions are repetitive: how long does a color service take, is there a deposit, what is the cancellation policy, do you carry a certain product line. A Calldesk agent can answer as the salon's AI assistant, ask which service and which provider, offer open slots on a connected calendar, and note special requests. It does not diagnose skin conditions or promise treatment outcomes. For waitlist-style fills, an outbound batch can ring clients on a list when a slot opens, using their first name and the opened time as variables. Staff review a summary of what was booked and changed.
callTypes: Booking a haircut, color or blowout with a preferred stylist
Massage and facial bookings, including couples and gift certificate redemptions
Rescheduling or cancelling within the shop's notice window
Bridal and event-party inquiries needing a consultation
Questions about service length, pricing ranges and deposit rules
Waitlist calls offering a last-minute slot to a client who asked

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks for calling the salon. I'm the salon's AI assistant. What service can I help you book?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: I want highlights, and I'd like Marisol if she's available.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Highlights with Marisol takes about two and a half hours. Have you been to the salon before?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Yes, she did my hair in the spring.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Welcome back. May I have your name?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks, Tess. Marisol has Thursday at 10 or Saturday at 1 open. Which is better for you?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: I've booked Saturday at 1. A reminder: appointments canceled with less than 24 hours' notice may carry a fee under the salon's policy. Is there anything Marisol should know ahead of time?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent

setupSteps: Create an agent from the appointment-booking template and list each service with its typical duration.
Connect a calendar for each stylist or treatment room you want the agent to book, or use one shared calendar and note preferred provider as a field.
Put your cancellation policy, deposit rules, product lines and gift certificate instructions in the knowledge base.
Add extraction fields for service, preferred provider, first-time or returning status and special requests.
Test booking and rescheduling scenarios, publish, and use batch calls for waitlist fills with client names as variables.

featuresUsed.howItHelps: Books a service into an open slot while the stylist is busy with a client.
Answers questions on service length, deposits and cancellation policy in your wording.
Records preferred provider, returning status and notes like a lighter color request.
Offers a freed-up slot to clients on your waitlist, naming each person and the time.
Shows what changed in the day's schedule so the front desk can check it at a glance.

considerations: Do not let the agent answer questions about skin conditions, allergic reactions or medical suitability of a treatment; refer those to the provider or the client's own doctor.
Late-cancellation fees and deposits are contract matters between you and the client. The agent should repeat your written policy and not invent exceptions.
Waitlist and promotional calls are outbound calls requiring the consent that applies in your location; ask your counsel about TCPA and local telemarketing rules.
Client information such as names and service history is personal data; review privacy requirements before connecting the agent to your client list.

faq.q: Can it book with a specific stylist?
faq.a: Yes, if each stylist has a calendar connected or you add the preferred stylist as a field for the front desk to confirm.
Not directly. It can explain how to buy one and take a request, but payment would be handled outside the call unless you build and verify a payment flow.
A cancellation path can free the calendar slot and log it, and a waitlist batch can then call clients who asked for earlier times.
It repeats the descriptions you provide. It should not promise results or medical benefits.

faq.q: Will clients know it is an AI?
faq.a: The sample call says so in the greeting. You can keep that line and offer a transfer to the front desk for anyone who prefers a person.
